title: Immunization Services Revenue Cycle Rule — Plan-Check Scheduling Allowance
content:
Revenue Cycle rule for Immunization Services at Kestrel Pharmacy: the plan-check allowance taken into Kestrel's scheduling allowance when a phone appointment is set for the next dose of a vaccination series.

## Rule

The plan-check allowance is **2 days** where the patient's active insurance plan is not a government program and two or more of the patient's claims were rejected in the last 3 calendar months, **1 day** where the active plan is not a government program and exactly one claim was rejected in the last 3 calendar months, and nothing otherwise.

## Records the rule reads

Both conditions are read from the patient's **Prescription Insurance on File** records:

- **the active plan** — the insurance plan on the patient's profile in active status, and whether its plan class is a government program (a federal or state health care program) as the plan class records it;
- **rejected claims** — the claim entries logged as rejected against the patient's insurance plans. A rejected claim lies within the last 3 calendar months when fewer than 3 whole calendar months separate its date from today.

## Condition table

| Active plan on file | Plan class a government program | Claims rejected in the last 3 calendar months | Plan-check allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | two or more | 2 days |
| yes | no | exactly one | 1 day |
| yes | no | none | nothing |
| yes | yes | any number | nothing |
| no active plan | not relevant | any number | nothing |

## Points of judgement

- **Is the count per plan?** The count is of the patient's rejected claims, whichever of the patient's plans they were billed to.
- **Where is the 3-month line?** With today taken, hypothetically, as 20 May: a rejection dated 21 February is 2 whole calendar months back and counts; a rejection dated 20 February is 3 whole calendar months back and does not.
- **Hypothetical case.** A patient's active plan is of a class that is not a government program, and two claims were rejected in April with today in May: the plan-check allowance is 2 days. Had the active plan been a government program class, the allowance would be nothing whatever the rejections.
